correctness.rationale: Exact claim is restricted to integers 3<=p<=15 for the corrected transition tables. The finite power automaton BFS layers from the full state set exhaust every reachable subset before any singleton; its shortest-path counts distinguish letter labels and count every shortest reset word. A distinct inverse-image BFS uses reversed subset transitions. The two explicit words target q_2 with length 3p^2+4p-1. Reconstructed state tables and independent forward BFS for p=3..9 returned precisely the reported minimum length, count two, and subset counts (199,597,1587,3951,9454,21998,50157). The source forward and reverse programs and witness code were inspected; much larger p=10..15 exhaustive outputs were not independently rerun. This is a finite exact enumeration, not an all-p lower-bound proof.

value.rationale: The corrected Figure 3 family is a concrete synchronizing-automata threshold example with a published global upper bound and an open exact sharpness issue. Exhaustive exact sharpness for thirteen consecutive parameters plus the complete surprising two-word minimizer classification gives a meaningful, reproducible finite cutoff and distinguishes global reset length from pair-compression claims. It does not masquerade as a solution for all p.
